title: Emergency shim for heterogeneous model fanout rate limiter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden increases in first-byte latency and token/sec drops across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private during heterogeneous model fanout workloads. Symptoms began 2026-03-08 23:00 UTC and correlate with a small subset of requests that fan out to >3 model variants and long contexts. Impact: elevated TTFT (median +220ms on affected routes), sustained token/sec drop ~35% for those requests, customer escalations from two enterprise VPC customers and one high-traffic hosted customer.

Observed behavior:
- Requests that concurrently invoke 3+ variants (short prompt + long context) sometimes stall at prefetch/warmup step and never progress to token emission for ~1.2-3s before fallback triggers.
- Router logs show asymmetric enqueue/backpressure: one model variant's rate limiter enters spike-protect mode, causing upstream queueing and head-of-line blocking for co-located requests.
- Kernel selector occasionally chooses quantized kernel with heavy warmup cost for the variant leading to serialization/affinity collisions.

Root cause hypothesis: A combination of conservative per-variant rate-limiter thresholds, the fanout coordinator's synchronous prefetch-on-demand, and a kernel warmup path that is single-threaded for some quantized variants leads to cascading head-of-line blocking under heterogeneous fanout. This manifests as TTFT spikes and lower tokens/sec for the entire request group.

Proposed emergency mitigation (short-lived shim):
1) Soft prewarm proxy: intercept fanout requests and apply a lightweight admission that converts full synchronous fanout into staggered preheat windows (25ms spacing by default) for variants marked as "heavy-warmup".
2) Per-request soft-leaky-bucket: allow limited burst to variants while throttling sustained concurrent warmups from the same tenant by token-bucket per-customer-per-model-class.
3) Fast fallback prioritization: if a variant does not respond within 450ms, automatically route remaining tokens to a pre-configured low-latency compatible variant (model aliasing).
4) Telemetry toggles and metrics: emit granular counters (prefetch_delay_ms, shim_throttled, fallback_invoked) and add to console dashboard for affected routes.

Rollout plan:
- Canary 1% traffic (hosted) for 2 hours, evaluate TTFT, tokens/sec, and error rate.
- Expand to 10% across hosted and Dedicated low-risk regions for 4 hours.
- 25% with Private customers by opt-in (contact SEs) while monitoring VPC logs.
- Full rollout once baseline improves and no regressions seen for 24 hours.

Testing & Validation:
- Microbench harness: synthetic fanout workload that reproduces warmup serialization; baseline vs shim to confirm TTFT median drop back to baseline within 20ms and tokens/sec restored to within 95% of normal.
- Integration: run against a set of canonical enterprise prompts used by escalated customers.

Operational runbook (short):
- Toggle shim via feature-flag gate (ff.platform.fanout_shim) and per-tenant override.
- If tokens/sec drops or error rate >0.5% on canary: rollback FF and revert routing.
- For persistent issues: apply emergency kernel fallback to non-quantized kernel for affected variant (manual) and scale up dedicated capacity for the tenant.

Postmortem actions:
- Replace synchronous prefetch with asynchronous preheat for the fanout coordinator (medium-term engineering task).
- Revisit kernel warmup parallelism for quantized kernels (research/infra cycle).
- Add per-variant warmup heuristics to model catalog metadata to avoid blind fanouts.

Links & artifacts:
- Incident bridge notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-08-fanout-latency
- Canary PR (shim implementation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8742
- Synthetic harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/fanout-synth
- Customer tickets: CID-44312, CID-44318, CID-44325
